topic: ‘Shark Tank’ Star Daymond John Invests in Ultimate Longevity Center

facts.label: Story
facts.value: ‘Shark Tank’ Star Daymond John Invests in Ultimate Longevity Center

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Ultimate longevity Center has sold more than 350 franchise territories globally, with its first locations set to open in January. The longevity franchise launched by Gary Brecka and Anthony Geisler has sold more than 350 franchise territories globally, with its first locations set to open in January “Shark Tank” star and entrepreneur Daymond John is investing in four Ultimate Longevity Centers, joining forces with Gary Brecka and Anthony Geisler as the fast-growing longevity franchise prepares to open its first locations. Ultimate Longevity Center (ULC) , part of Geisler’s Sequel Brands portfolio, has sold more than 350 franchise territories globally since launching franchise sales earlier this year, including 200 in its first four months, according to the brand. The brand’s first locations are slated to open in January 2027 in Arizona, Colorado, Florida and Southern California. ULC is also expanding internationally, with plans for 50 locations in Australia . John, the founder of apparel brand Fubu and a longtime investor on ABC’s “Shark Tank,” will become an owner-investor in four ULC locations. Financial terms of the investments weren’t disclosed. “Gary Brecka has changed my life and my wife Heather’s life for the better. Period,” John said. “This is about more than investing in four centers.

topic: Why Member Retention Gets Harder as Fitness Businesses Grow

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Why Member Retention Gets Harder as Fitness Businesses Grow

facts.label: Article
facts.value: Pam Kufahl, VP of Marketing & Communications, HFA Guest – Jody Hinman, North America Director of Sales, Hapana Growth brings new challenges to member retention. What works when an owner is personally connected to every member at one location doesn’t always translate across five, 10 or 20. As fitness businesses expand, maintaining a consistent member experience, retaining great staff, and understanding what’s happening at each location become increasingly important. Jody Hinman, North America Director of Sales at Hapana, joins Pam Kufahl to explore where retention challenges emerge as businesses scale, what successful operators are doing differently in the first 30 days of membership, and how location-level insights can help identify at-risk members before they walk away.

topic: Club Operators Can Build Community By Designing for Social Dose, Not Just Exercise Dose

facts.label: Story
facts.value: Club Operators Can Build Community By Designing for Social Dose, Not Just Exercise Dose

facts.label: Article
facts.value: A new narrative review on group-based exercise and loneliness gives health club operators a research-backed framework for building social connection into the way they program and run classes. In this episode, hosts Luke Carlson and Rachel Chonko break down the paper that examines the components, mechanisms and design principles that allow group-based physical activity to reduce loneliness and what it means for group fitness design. For operators who talk constantly about community but struggle to define it, the paper offers specific elements to build into the member experience. Club Solutions Magazine · Club Operators Can Build Community By Designing for Social Dose, Not Just Exercise Dose What This Episode Covers: This review synthesizes existing research on psychology, loneliness and group exercise instead of comparing outcomes between study groups. The top takeaways from the paper include: Exercise does and social dose are distinct concepts, with social dose referring to the structured opportunities for connection built into group activity. Being around other people isn’t the same as feeling connected to them, as a member can attend a crowded class and still feel lonely. Belongingness, social identity and peer support emerge as three interwoven pathways that appear to drive social connection in group exercise.

en.headline: Club Operators Can Build Community By Designing for Social Dose, Not Just Exercise Dose
